references.text: The Mosaic law regarding the brother-in-law's duty (levirate marriage): If brothers live together and one of them dies without having a son, the widow of the deceased shall not marry a stranger. Her husband's brother shall go in to her, take her as his wife, and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law toward her. [ref:5 Mos 25:5-6|Deuteronomy 25:5-6] is the direct basis for the Sadducees' question in Luke 20:28.

An early example of levirate marriage in practice: Judah tells Onan to go in to his brother's wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law, so that he may raise up offspring for his brother ([ref:1 Mos 38:8|Genesis 38:8]). This illustrates the custom that Moses later codified in the law.

Boaz explains the principle of raising up the name of the deceased over his inheritance through marriage to his widow ([ref:Rut 4:5|Ruth 4:5]). This is a practical application of the levirate law to which the Sadducees refer.
Naomi refers to the tradition of levirate marriage when she says that she has no more sons who can become husbands for her daughters-in-law ([ref:Rut 1:11-13|Ruth 1:11-13]).
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:24|Matthew 22:24] where the Sadducees ask Jesus the same question with almost identical wording regarding the Mosaic law's provision on levirate marriage.
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:19|Mark 12:19] with the Sadducees' reference to Moses' law that a brother shall take his deceased brother's wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
